purpose: 3D wall-section references for Meshy; no image is used as a repeating surface tile

prompts.factory-wall-lower: Use case: stylized-concept. Production reference for ONE solid 3D architectural wall module to be reconstructed with Meshy, NOT a texture tile, not a seamless swatch. A complete rectangular interior wall section from a derelict industrial warehouse skatepark, 10 metres wide, 7 metres high and about 0.45 metres thick. Front view with only a very small 8-degree view of its right thickness; complete edges and silhouette fully inside the frame. Solid wall: NO doors, NO windows, NO holes through it, NO attached floor or roof, NO pillars. Straight flush top, bottom and sides suitable for assembly between existing steel columns; wear and small chips do not remove the rectangular footprint. Most of the broad face is aged warm ivory lime plaster, lower quarter faded petrol-blue painted masonry, layered torn paint and a few deep irregular cracks. Localized exposed reddish brick at one lower corner and a broad patch near the opposite upper edge, irregular chipped plaster with real modeled thickness and raised worn edges. A restrained original teal and dirty coral handstyle spraypaint scrawl occupies a small part of the lower third, no readable brand name. Use large, art-directed shapes of wear and quiet intact plaster between damaged areas, not uniform noise. Believable slightly chunky geometry and tactile weathering in the spirit of Crash Bandicoot 4 environment shapes and THPS 1+2 abandoned factories. Neutral diffuse studio illumination, no baked cast shadows, plain neutral gray background, no scenery, people, captions, watermark or perspective cropping. Render the full solid wall section as a game-ready object, not a material sample.
prompts.factory-wall-upper: Use case: stylized-concept. Production reference for ONE solid 3D architectural wall module to be reconstructed with Meshy, NOT a texture tile, not a seamless swatch. A complete rectangular upper infill wall section from a derelict industrial warehouse, 10 metres wide, 8 metres high and about 0.45 metres thick. Front view with only a very small 8-degree view of its right thickness; complete silhouette inside frame. Solid wall: NO windows, doors, holes, roof, floor or pillars. Straight flush top, bottom and side boundaries suited for assembly around existing tall factory windows. Broad weathered pale warm-gray plaster over aged brick, with a large irregular area of missing plaster exposing brick along the lower right, a diagonal hairline crack and a few sculpted delaminated plaster plates near the upper left. Localized vertical damp/rust streaks descending from two small old iron wall anchors, soot near one upper corner, generous quiet plaster areas, no evenly scattered noise. Real shallow geometry at the chipped plaster-to-brick transitions, subtly bevelled edges, physically convincing thin rectangular solid. Rich readable stylized shape language inspired by Crash Bandicoot 4 with the industrial material wear of THPS 1+2. No graffiti text, no logos or signs. Neutral diffuse studio light with no baked cast shadows, plain gray background, no environment or floor plane, no characters, labels or watermark. An architectural object reference, not a repeating surface texture.
